messages:
Sam (sales): Heads-up — ACME asked for an "anchor" pricing pilot. They want a temporary per-token floor for 90 days + a pool of 'pilot credits' that map to reserved capacity behavior. Asking us to propose structure by EOD. Their workload: embeddings-heavy + occasional large text-gen spikes. Ping @Riya for prioritization.

Anya (support): Quick context: they are on trial, ~2M tokens/week today, forecasted to hit 10M/wk during peak. Main concern is unpredictable overage bills. They want simpler invoice lines (pilot credits) and a predictable cap. Raised support ticket #4521 with logs & usage pattern.

triage-bot: Created PM task PROD-789, linked support ticket #4521.

Riya (PM): Thanks. We need to clarify requirements before we scope: 1) exact blending/discount ask (they mentioned ~30% off list for first 6m if commit X) 2) how credits convert to reserved capacity (1 credit = ? GPU-minutes? tokens?) 3) overage policy and soft/hard caps. Proposed MVP: pilot promo credits + invoice SKU + monitoring/alerts. What are launch criteria and acceptance tests?

Luca (revops): Top-level economics: rough calc — if we take 30% off list on 10M tokens/wk for 26 weeks that's material. Formula: revenue_delta = (list_rate * tokens) - (discounted_rate * tokens). Need inputs: list_rate (per-token), expected token mix (embeddings vs gen), and expected uplift/churn. Operational ask: prefer prepaid credits (applied as invoice line). Credits expire at pilot end. Accounting can handle short promos but need contract code + legal sign-off.

Maya (prod): Engineering notes: We can implement this as a billing/promo construct without touching serving for MVP — i.e., promo credits that auto-apply to invoices. Exposing an actual blended per-token rate at the API/runtime level is more invasive (impacts metering & reporting). Mapping credits -> reserved behavior (guaranteed throughput) needs Dedicated or explicit burst policies; we can't promise isolation on Hosted. Suggest scope for pilot: - Issue "pilot_credit" SKU that deducts tokens/costs - Implement soft overage cap (e.g., block charge above 2x baseline + notify) - Provide Console alerts and cost dashboards for the account. Launch criteria: legal ok, billing workflows tested in staging, support playbook, and spike test to 2x expected peak.

Maya (prod): Example promo payload we can use for billing team / staging:

```
promo = {
  "sku": "pilot_anchor_acme_90d",
  "tokens_allocated": "150000000",
  "valid_from": "2026-04-01",
  "valid_until": "2026-06-30",
  "overage_cap_multiplier": "2.0"
}
```

Sam (sales): That MVP approach sounds reasonable. Can engineering commit to soft-cap alerts (Console & email) within 48h of scope lock so I can promise ACME notification windows? :pray:

Maya (prod): We can add alerting hooks (Console route + webhook) in ~48h after scope lock, assuming no other high-priority work blocks. Hard guarantees (reserved throughput) require Dedicated purchase.

Riya (PM): I'll draft a short PRD with acceptance criteria: 1) invoice shows pilot SKU, 2) credits auto-applied, 3) overage behavior: soft-cap + manual uplift flow, 4) telemetry: tokens consumed vs credits and unit economics dashboard. Target: staged rollout to single account, monitor 2 weeks post-launch. Assigning action items: @Luca to produce revenue sensitivity, @Maya for engineering estimate, @Anya for support playbook & customer comms.

Anya (support): I'll prepare the support playbook and email templates. Will include escalation steps if customer hits soft cap, and a checklist for manual uplift.

Luca (revops): I'll run sensitivity with two scenarios (30% discount vs 15% discount) and include churn/uplift assumptions. Expect to post numbers by EOD.

triage-bot: PROD-789 updated: status=needs-estimate, assignee=Maya.

Sam (sales): Cool, I'll loop ACME in after PRD draft. Thanks all :)
